title: Add retention verification metrics (ttl_lag_seconds, purge_rows_deleted, purge_failures)
author: Caleb Johnson
release_notes: Adds Prometheus metrics for retention TTL lag and purge job outcomes; enables SRE dashboards/alerts for retention enforcement verification.
body:
## Summary
This PR emits a minimal set of metrics required for retention enforcement verification and customer/compliance reporting SLOs:
- `redwood_retention_ttl_lag_seconds` (gauge) — how far behind TTL enforcement is vs policy target
- `redwood_retention_purge_rows_deleted_total` (counter) — number of rows deleted by purge jobs
- `redwood_retention_purge_failures_total` (counter) — purge failures by store + reason

These metrics are produced by the purge job framework and the store-specific TTL deleters (request logs + audit logs in v1). They are designed to be low-cardinality and safe to alert on. This unblocks ENG-18452 (verification dashboards/alerts) and standardizes signals across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

## Motivation / Context
SRE and Security asked for a consistent way to:
1) prove retention policies are being applied (TTL lag trending to ~0)
2) catch silent failures/backlog growth after maintenance windows
3) support evidence collection ("show me the last 30 days of purge success + lag")

Prior to this PR we had logs for purge runs but no stable metrics surface. This PR adds metrics instrumentation and defines label conventions aligned with our observability standards.

## Metrics details
### 1) TTL lag
Name: `redwood_retention_ttl_lag_seconds`
Type: gauge
Labels:
- `store` (enum): `request_logs` | `audit_logs` (v1)
- `region` (cloud region id, e.g. `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`)
- `tenant_tier` (enum): `hosted` | `dedicated` | `private`

Definition:
`ttl_lag_seconds = max(0, now - (max_deleted_timestamp))` where `max_deleted_timestamp` is the newest record timestamp that the purge job has successfully advanced past. This matches how the deleters operate (delete by time window / watermark).

Notes:
- We intentionally do NOT label by tenant_id, cluster_id, model, route, or job_run_id.
- For multi-tenant stores, the lag is computed at the store+region level (worst-case watermark), which is what SRE wants for paging. Tenant-level drift is handled separately via policy-drift metrics/logs in the retention policy service.

### 2) Purge rows deleted
Name: `redwood_retention_purge_rows_deleted_total`
Type: counter
Labels:
- `store`
- `region`
- `result` (enum): `success` | `noop`

Notes:
- `noop` is used when a job run finds nothing to delete in the evaluated window.

### 3) Purge failures
Name: `redwood_retention_purge_failures_total`
Type: counter
Labels:
- `store`
- `region`
- `reason` (enum, bounded): `db_timeout` | `db_throttled` | `permission_denied` | `unknown`

Implementation details:
- Failure reasons are mapped from a small set of known error classes; anything else maps to `unknown`.
- We increment failures once per job run attempt (not per row) to avoid overcounting when a single error aborts a batch.

## Implementation notes
- Instrumentation sits in `purge_job_runner` so every TTL deleter gets the same metric surface.
- Store-specific deleters provide:
  - `store_name` (enum)
  - `watermark_before`/`watermark_after`
  - `rows_deleted`
- `ttl_lag_seconds` is updated on successful runs using `watermark_after`.

Example snippet (illustrative):
```
retentionMetrics.ttlLagSeconds
  .withLabels(store, region, tenantTier)
  .set(Math.max(0, nowEpochSeconds - watermarkAfterEpochSeconds));

retentionMetrics.purgeRowsDeletedTotal
  .withLabels(store, region, rowsDeleted > 0 ? "success" : "noop")
  .inc(rowsDeleted);

retentionMetrics.purgeFailuresTotal
  .withLabels(store, region, reason)
  .inc(1);
```

## Files / Areas changed
- `packages/observability/src/metrics/retention.ts` — metric definitions + label validation helpers
- `services/purge-jobs/src/runner/purge_job_runner.ts` — instrumentation hooks
- `services/request-logs/src/ttl/request_logs_ttl_deleter.ts` — returns watermark/rows_deleted
- `services/audit-logs/src/ttl/audit_logs_ttl_deleter.ts` — returns watermark/rows_deleted
- `packages/observability/src/metrics/registry.ts` — register new metrics
- `services/*/README.md` — doc notes for operators (metric names + label sets)
- `tests/observability/retention_metrics.test.ts` — unit tests around label boundedness + failure reason mapping

## Testing
- Unit:
  - verifies all metric labels are bounded / enum-like
  - verifies unknown exceptions map to `reason=unknown`
- Integration:
  - runs purge runner against a local test DB with synthetic timestamps; asserts counters/gauges change as expected

## Rollout / Ops
- Safe to deploy behind existing purge jobs; metrics are additive.
- No changes to retention policy behavior.
- Suggested initial alerts (to be implemented in ENG-18452 / observability-pack):
  - page if `ttl_lag_seconds > 6h` for 30m (per store+region)
  - warn if `purge_failures_total` increases > N in 15m

## Checklist
- [x] Labels reviewed for cardinality (no tenant_id)
- [x] Tests added
- [x] Docs updated (metric names)
- [x] Backwards compatible

## Notes / Follow-ups
- Tenant-level drift/override metrics will live in the control plane (separate work) and should not be added here to avoid high-cardinality.
- Once dashboards land, we should add runbook links in the alert annotations (ENG-18452).

commits: obs: define retention verification metrics + bounded labels
purge-jobs: emit ttl lag + delete/failure counters from runner
request-logs: return watermark and rows_deleted for ttl deleter
audit-logs: return watermark and rows_deleted for ttl deleter
tests: add retention metrics label + reason mapping coverage
review_thread: Allison Grant: Please confirm we’re not labeling by tenant_id anywhere (including derived labels). Also want a hard-coded allowlist for `reason` values so we don’t explode cardinality on exception messages.
Caleb Johnson (author): Confirmed: no tenant_id labels. Added `mapFailureReason()` with an enum allowlist and tests; removed any propagation of raw error strings.

Sean Gallagher: TTL lag definition—are we using watermark-after from the deleter? For paging I want this to reflect the oldest remaining data (worst-case), not average. Also, can we add `noop` vs `success` to rows_deleted so we can see if jobs are running but not doing work?

Caleb Johnson (author): Yes: using the deleter’s watermark-after (advances monotonically). For multi-tenant stores it’s store-level watermark (worst-case). Added `result` label to rows_deleted_total with `noop` when 0 rows deleted.

Logan Wright: The gauge naming should include unit. `ttl_lag_seconds` is good. Please make sure we register this in the shared registry so dashboards can discover it in all services. Also, can we document label sets in a README for SRE?
Caleb Johnson (author): Done. Registered in `packages/observability` registry. Added short metric docs to service READMEs and a comment block in `retention.ts`.
Jordan Lee: Anything here interacts with policy evaluation cache? I’m fine as long as this stays in data plane and doesn’t pull control plane dependencies.
Caleb Johnson (author): No control plane deps; the runner only receives `store` + `region` + `tier` context from existing config and uses deleter watermarks.
Allison Grant: Approved after changes. Please keep label sets stable (dashboards/alerts depend on this).
Sean Gallagher: Approved. Would like follow-up to wire into dashboards and create paging thresholds.
